items.title: Supreme Court upholds Karnataka HC order permitting bike taxi services

items.summary: A three-year-old tigress, T138, was soft-released into an enclosure in West Bengal's Buxa Tiger Reserve on October 2 and reportedly walked into the wild two days later. The move resulted from a joint initiative of the West Bengal Forest Department and National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), following a recovery plan prepared with the Wildlife Institute of India over roughly a decade ago that included improving the prey base by bringing sambar deer from Jaldapara. Buxa had recorded no tigers in an 2018 all-India estimation, with camera traps later detecting one male tiger only in late 2021; Chief Wildlife Warden Pradeep Vyas attributed the decline to poaching and biotic interference since around 1970. To let T138 acclimatise while radio-collared, officials restricted tourism at Rajabhatkhawa range from September 30 initially, later extending it. Residents of 18 forest villages protested with a sit-in dharna alleging livelihood losses; Ayan Naidu of the Maha Gram Sabha Joutha Sangram Committee said restrictions affect more than 10,000 people and cancelled bookings during October's earning season. Protesters also demand removal of the Rajabhatkhawa toll gate (₹480 per vehicle plus ₹150 per person), implementation of the Forest Rights Act, 2006, declaration of forest settlements as revenue villages, and questioned whether villagers could be relocated for reintroduction-linked dolomite mining. More tigers are slated for release in coming months without official details; senior officials declined to comment. Buxa spans 760.87 sq km in Alipurduar district with landscape connectivity to Bhutan forests, Kochugaon and Manas Tiger Reserve (Assam), and Jaldapara. T138 is currently at Chuniajhora area of Hathipota range.
items.title: Forest villagers protest tourism curbs after tiger translocation to Buxa Tiger Reserve

items.summary: Political analyst Sareen argues that dividing Punjab and Sindh into smaller provinces, as floated by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, could weaken established parties like the PPP and PML-N while making regional leaders dependent on the military establishment. He compared the armed forces to a political party akin to China's Communist Party, noting that losing Karachi would render Sindh politically meaningless for the PPP. Sareen questioned whether a referendum on the plan might bypass constitutional procedures, characterizing the restructuring as driven by an 'undeclared dictator' and warning it could trigger resistance and instability. He cited mineral wealth in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and provincial revenue-sharing arrangements—where provinces currently receive around 57% of the divisible pool—as possible motives behind greater federal control, calling greed boundless. On India's interests, Sareen said controlled Pakistani instability would benefit India but cautioned that an uncontrolled crisis in a country of roughly 250 million people could pose serious challenges for New Delhi. All claims are attributed to Sareen; the 57% figure and population size reflect his reported statements.
items.title: Analyst Sareen warns Pakistan's proposed smaller provinces would entrench military rule

items.summary: In a September 8 case (year reported as 2026), the Madras High Court dismissed Kalaiselvi's claim to 2.5 acres of land originally owned by Mr Arunachala Chetty, holding that it was self-acquired rather than ancestral property under Hindu law and thus governed by Section 14(2) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956. The land had been bequeathed via a November 10, 1953 will giving his wife Smt Unnamalaiammal a life interest with an express condition against sale or gift, ultimately passing to son Veerappan; after she and Veerappan executed a February 26, 1975 gift settlement deed transferring it to Ganga (Veerappan's second wife), who sold it in 1996. Kalaiselvi, Veerappan's daughter from his first marriage, argued the land was ancestral and that her stepmother had no right to sell it. The court relied on C.N. Arunachala Mudaliar vs C.A. Muruganatha Mudaliar (AIR 1953 SC 495), which held that a will beneficiary's property character depends on the testator's intention: absolute enjoyment yields separate property, while intent to benefit the branch or partition yields joint family property. Rajani Tandale of 1 Finance told ET Wealth Online that courts today usually treat silent or vague wills as creating separate property for the beneficiary and advised drafting clear words stating whether a bequest is separate (with full rights to sell, gift, mortgage or bequeath) or HUF/joint-family property with birthrights. Yogendra Aldak of Lakshmikumaran & Sridharan told ET Wealth Online that under Section 30 a Hindu father may leave self-acquired property to anyone without the son's objection, while intestate succession passes through Class I heirs (widow, sons, daughters, mother) each taking an equal share as absolute individual property. The item notes these inheritance principles but does not establish them as universal law beyond the cited cases and expert statements.
items.title: Madras High Court rules disputed land was self-acquired, not ancestral

items.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India reported a market capitalisation of Rs 5,54,499 crore ($59.65 billion) as of Friday, crossing the Rs 5 lakh crore mark on Monday amid renewed interest in large-cap stocks. The Economic Times attributes this milestone to NSE's operating EBITDA margin of 66.9%, which sits at the upper end of the 53-80% range across five global exchange operators; these figures are presented as comparisons rather than established causes, and the ranking itself is a claim from an unverified source. The article notes that NASDAQ's market cap stood at $57.6 billion and Hong Kong Exchanges & Clearing (HKEX) at $57.38 billion on unspecified dates, though it does not specify whether these are current or historical values. Separately, NSE shares rose 2.8% to an intraday high of Rs 2,251 per share on the BSE after a three-session rally that added roughly 8%, making NSE India's ninth-largest listed company by market capitalisation ahead of Kotak Mahindra Bank (Rs 5.03 lakh crore) and Life Insurance Corporation of India (Rs 5.15 lakh crore). The stock had risen about 26% in the month versus a 10% Sensex gain, with shares up roughly 23% from their September 24 listing price of Rs 1,785; these are reported movements rather than forecasts or conclusions.
items.title: NSE claims world's fifth-largest listed stock exchange by market capitalisation

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation's first Civilizational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila, New Delhi, running from 20th to 22nd November. The forum follows a proposal Modi made at the 2025 SCO Summit in Tianjin, China, and includes ten member nations. An invitation extended to Pakistani minister Musadik Malik drew questions from the Congress party, which Ministries clarified as a protocol obligation that does not change India's bilateral stance.
items.title: Modi inaugurates first SCO Civilizational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi

items.summary: A Bharatiya Janata Party leader criticised the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (AITC) government in Tamil Nadu across several governance issues. He questioned the government's approach to the Supreme Court ruling that permitted interim lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Tirupparankundram Hill under strict security and supervision conditions, amid ongoing historical and political disputes over the ritual. The leader also raised law-and-order concerns by citing a major heroin seizure in Madhavaram alongside alleged police intelligence failures, questioned why confidential investment data was shared by the Industries Department, and likened governance problems to scenes from a video game.
items.title: BJP leader criticises Tamil Nadu government on Thirupparankundram dispute and law enforcement

items.summary: The FlightGlobal-published 2027 World Air Forces directory reports that the Indian Air Force has 32 active Rafales out of the 36 it had purchased. The previous November 2025 edition listed 35, a reduction attributed to Cirium's tracking methodology rather than confirmed combat losses: aircraft can be dropped from the active list after long-term depot overhauls or structural repairs with no sightings within a 12-month window. FlightGlobal compiled its figures from data gathered by Cirium using public sightings and open-source defence reporting; it did not explain why specific jets were deemed inactive, nor does an inactive designation imply loss in combat. The directory also cut Pakistan's Saab Erieye count to seven from nine after the May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, though it listed 263 active Su-30MKIs for India even as other reports put that fleet at roughly 258 to 260. Retired Air Marshal Narmdeshwar Tiwari called the directory's claim "patently false," arguing its sources had since recorded jets flying in exercises and disputing a prior source report of an Indian pilot taken prisoner; India's Ministry of Defence has not commented, though officials quoted by The Hindu questioned the data's authenticity. Separately, conflicting accounts surround aircraft losses from Operation Sindoor: Defence Secretary RK Singh denied that multiple Rafales were shot down while French Air Force chief General Jérôme Bellanger cited evidence for three Indian losses (a Rafale, an Su-30MKI and a Mirage 2000), India claimed five Pakistani F-16s and JF-17s downed, and Pakistan acknowledged airbase strikes without confirming aircraft losses. In February the government approved buying 114 more Rafales for the Air Force plus 26 Rafale Marines for the Navy.
items.title: FlightGlobal's 2027 World Air Forces directory lists India's active Rafale count at 32, down from a prior edition's 35 and its purchased total of 36

items.summary: Manipur police reported at least eight deaths over three days, with two on Friday, one on Thursday and five on November 18, allegedly following consumption of adulterated liquor in the Chakpikarong sub-division and adjoining areas of Chandel district. The exact cause remains medically unestablished and is under investigation; police advised the public to exercise caution and avoid locally brewed or doubtful-origin alcohol until further notice. Police said the liquor was reportedly procured from Sugnu in Kakching district, noting there is no known local brewing or manufacturing of wine in Chandel.
items.title: Eight deaths linked to spurious liquor in Manipur's Chandel district

items.summary: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, addressing the Defence Estates Organisation's centenary celebrations in New Delhi on Friday, said military cantonments should be modernised while preserving their green heritage of forests and land. He stated that development must not come at the cost of this identity, with clean, forested, green environments remaining central to what distinguishes military from civilian areas. Birla called for greater use of artificial intelligence and digital records in defence land management, noting the organisation safeguards more than 17 lakh acres while preventing encroachments. He acknowledged the department works with limited manpower and resources but praised its officers; he urged combining institutional heritage with younger professionals' technological capabilities to build a more efficient management ecosystem.
items.title: Birla urges cantonment modernisation that preserves original character

items.summary: Congress MP Imran Masood claimed Mohammed Siraj was omitted from India's playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand because of his religion, arguing that despite good performance he was dropped over discrimination. Union minister Kiren Rijiju rejected this as merit-based selection unaffected by religion or caste, BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused Congress of vote-bank politics, and BJP leader Boora Narsaiah Goud called the statement unfortunate while BJP spokesperson TR Sriniwas attacked Masood for repeatedly raising Hindu-Muslim issues. Team management attributed Siraj's exclusion to bowling combination preferences and conditions at Wellington rather than any religious consideration.
items.title: Congress MP alleges religious bias in Siraj's Test exclusion; BJP rebuts

items.summary: An economics article by Sarika Rachuri argues that while female education is widely cited as a development imperative, it does not automatically raise women's employment. The author notes the national female literacy rate rose from 8.86 per cent in 1951 to 64.63 per cent at the 2011 Census, with urban rates of 79.11 per cent and wide state disparities between Kerala (highest) and Rajasthan (lowest). A State-level correlation test found a negligible rank relationship (-0.05) between female literacy and the female labour force participation rate, which ranges from 4.1 per cent in Bihar to 50 per cent in Chhattisgarh; the author attributes this disconnect to government policies that improved access but not employability or skills, alongside high dropout rates of 4.1, 4.5 and 17.8 per cent at primary, upper-primary and secondary levels respectively. The piece invokes a U-shaped hypothesis attributed to Claudia Goldin: lower-educated women in poorer households work out of necessity while middle-income educated women withdraw for domestic care, with affluent higher-education women re-entering the workforce; Rachuri concludes that literacy alone cannot close the skill gap and calls for further investment in women's skills. The article is an opinion piece drawing on a research paper by its author published in volume 64 of The Administrator, which went live in November 2026.
items.title: Female literacy in India has not translated into higher female labour force participation
